sections.Kurzabstract: The Discontinuation Success Scale (DSS) assesses the subjective discontinuation success of patients who take antipsychotics or antidepressants. It consists of 24 items distributed across three subscales ((1) Subjective discontinuation success, (2) Positive discontinuation effects, (3) Negative discontinuation effects). Reliability: No information available. Validity: Factorial and criterion validity as well as measurement invariance between persons taking antidepressants and antipsychotics were computed.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The diagnostic aim of the Discontinuation Success Scale (DSS) is to quantify the subjective discontinuation success of patients who take antipsychotics or antidepressants.
sections.Aufbau: The test consists of 24 items, to which agreement can be indicated on a five-point Likert scale (1 = "stimme überhaupt nicht zu", 5 = "stimme voll und ganz zu").
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The DSS was developed based on the experiences of people with actual experience of medication discontinuation, and the items were tested by means of exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis. In addition, significant associations were found between the DSS scale scores and objective discontinuation success on the one hand and subjective well-being on the other.
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: No information available.
Validity: Factorial validation with the requirement that each factor has at least four items with loadings > 0.60. EFA to validate the dimensional structure of the DSS. CFA to validate model fit based on the CFI. Testing of measurement invariance between antidepressants and antipsychotics. Testing of criterion validity using the associations between DSS scores and objective discontinuation success in relation to well-being.
Norms: No reference values are available.
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund: The Discontinuation Success Scale (DSS; Lincoln, Sommer, Könemund & Schlier, 2021) is used to assess subjective discontinuation success after discontinuing psychotropic medication (antipsychotics and antidepressants). The DSS was developed to assess subjective discontinuation success in a differentiated way. The questionnaire can be used both in the therapeutic accompaniment of discontinuation success and to empirically investigate predictors of discontinuation success.
sections.Testkonzept/Testaufbau: The DSS comprises 24 items with three subscales - one for evaluating discontinuation success as such (subscale "Subjective discontinuation success"), one that assesses positive discontinuation effects (subscale "Positive discontinuation effects") and one that assesses negative discontinuation effects (subscale "Negative discontinuation effects"). The items are answered using a five-point Likert scale (1 = "stimme überhaupt nicht zu" to 5 = "stimme voll und ganz zu").
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus:
For each subscale, the average value is calculated by adding the raw item scores:
Subjective discontinuation success: (item_1 + item_2 + item_3 + (6-item_4) + (6-item_5) + item_8)/6
(Explanation: Since item 4 and item 5 are negatively keyed, a corresponding conversion is required here.)
Positive discontinuation effects: (item_6 + item_11 + item_13 + item_14 + item_15 + item_17 + item_22 + item_23 + item_24)/9
Negative discontinuation effects: (item_7 + item_9 + item_10 + item_12 + item_16 + item_18 + item_19+ item_20 + item_21)/9
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: Under "Scoring procedure", exact calculations are specified for all three subscales.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Scoring time is a few minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: The DSS (Lincoln et al., 2021) is available as a 24-item version in German and English. It should be noted that currently no results on validity are available for the English translation of the items.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The instrument is suitable for adults.
sections.Durchführung/Material: The materials include the documentation of the procedure as well as the questionnaire in German and English. A writing implement is needed to answer the items.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion:
The test person is instructed at the beginning of the test form with the following text:
„Im Folgenden finden Sie einige Aussagen, die auf Ihre Erfahrungen mit dem Absetzen Ihrer Medikamente zutreffen könnten – manche mehr, manche weniger. Bitte bewerten Sie vor dem Hintergrund Ihres letzten Absetzungsversuchs, inwieweit Sie jeder der folgenden Aussagen zustimmen.“
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge: There are no special administration requirements on the part of the test administrator.
sections.Testkonstruktion:
The DSS (Lincoln et al., 2021) was developed by means of exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA).
Item pool:
The item pool was developed based on (1) the current research literature on the topic, (2) subjective reports of people with personal discontinuation experience in online discussion forums (Herz, 2017) and (3) personal interviews with experts and with persons with personal discontinuation experience (Woitalla, 2017). The item pool contained 35 items.
Preliminary test versions:
The preliminary DSS contained 35 items. These were answered on a Likert scale (1 = "stimme überhaupt nicht zu" to 5 = "stimme voll und ganz zu"). Subjective well-being was assessed using the Well-Being Index [WHO-5].
Item selection criteria and techniques:
The factor-analytic validation consisted of four steps:
Visual inspection and analysis of the principal component analysis using the nFactors package; condition: each factor should have at least four items with a loading > 0.6.
Subsequently, EFA of the 35 items with a varimax rotation. Items with a factor loading < 0.3 were excluded. Items with loadings on different factors were excluded if they offered no added value in content for the scale.
Computation of a CFA to evaluate the model fit of the factor solution on the basis of the Comparative Fit Index (CFI, CFI > 0.95 = good fit, CFI > 0.90 = adequate fit), the Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA, RMSEA < 0.05 = good fit, RMSEA < 0.08 = adequate fit), and the Standardized Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR, SRMR < 0.08 = good fit).
Measurement of measurement invariance across antidepressants versus antipsychotics with the model-fit limits mentioned above and the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC, where lower values of a model based on the same data indicate a better fit).
Factor-analytic results:
Item extraction on the basis of the EFA loadings yielded 24 items that had a loading > 0.30 on their respective factor. A three-dimensional scale resulted, which reflects the subjective success of the exit, the positive effects and the negative consequences of the exit. A 24-item version showed adequate model fit for the participants who discontinued antidepressants and antipsychotics, respectively (see Table 1).

Measurement invariance:
To ensure sufficient group sizes (n > 100), the tests for invariance between the medication groups were based on one group that discontinued antidepressants and one group that discontinued either only antipsychotics or antipsychotics and antidepressants. Separate confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) with unconstrained loadings showed adequate fit for both groups (see Table 2).

sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: Owing to the questionnaire format, the standardized procedure and the written instruction, the instrument can claim objectivity with regard to its administration and scoring.
sections.Gütekriterien/Reliabilität: No information on reliability is available.
sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
Construct validity:
Construct validity was examined by means of exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis (see Tables 1 and 2).
Criterion validity:
To measure criterion validity, associations between the DSS scores and (1) achievement status (with three groups: persons who had implemented discontinuation; persons who had implemented it partially; persons who had not implemented it) and (2) well-being, measured with the Well-Being Index [WHO-5; Topp, Ostergaard, Sondergaard & Bech, 2015] (with two groups: high vs. low well-being), were computed by means of two-way ANOVAs.
Overall, the persons who had successfully discontinued (52.8 % of the total sample) achieved higher results with regard to the objectively perceived success of discontinuation, as well as perceived positive effects, compared with persons who had partially discontinued the medication (33.3 % of the sample) and those who had not discontinued successfully (13.1 % of the sample). In addition, persons who had successfully discontinued the medication reported perceiving fewer negative effects than persons who had partially or unsuccessfully discontinued the medication.
Since the test refers on the one hand to the objective success of discontinuation (i.e. the extent to which the goal of discontinuation was achieved) and on the other hand to the perceived psychological and physical consequences of discontinuation, criterion validity was tested for both aspects. These were measured by (1) whether the goal of the discontinuation attempt was achieved (= no medication intake at the end of the survey period) and (2) good subjective well-being.
The results imply that the success of discontinuation and a person's degree of well-being do not necessarily seem to be associated with each other. However, the subscales for the perceived positive and negative effects tend to discriminate between persons with higher or lower well-being. This is independent of the type of medication, although it could be shown that for persons who only wanted to discontinue antipsychotics, there seems to be no significant association between perceived well-being and the score achieved on the DSS scale.

sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten: The DSS is suitable as an instrument for future research aimed at identifying predictors of discontinuation success. If appropriate, it can also be used as a basis for a consultation within discontinuation counselling or accompaniment.
sections.Bewertung: Limitations of the scale are a lack of validation against an observer report of discontinuation success and the lack of information on test-retest reliability.
